files.purpose: Single shared NSPopover that shows a 300pt-wide hover card for a Hydra head mention in chat markdown: the persona glyph, its name in the persona colour, the helper agent's task text (max 3 lines) and a status line. files.purpose: The single shared transient NSPopover shown when a chat link is right-clicked, replacing the system text menu with house rows: an optional Merge row for a merge or pull request link (wearing the forge's favicon), then Open Link and Copy Link. Adds a local Escape key monitor so it dismisses like a menu.

files.purpose: Resolves the human title of a bare YouTube video link in chat so it renders as the video's own title instead of "youtube.com/watch". Recognizes the YouTube URL shapes, fetches titles at most once each from YouTube's public oEmbed endpoint (no API key), and keeps them in a lock-guarded store rather than @MainActor state because RichLink.build reads it off the main actor during cache warm-up.

state_owned: private var titles: [String: String] = [:] (video id -> title)
private var claimed = Set<String>() (ids whose fetch has been claimed or answered)
side_effects: Outbound network request: GET https://www.youtube.com/oembed?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3D<id>&format=json via URLSession.shared
Mutates the in-memory title cache under an NSLock
No disk writes, no keychain, no timers
platform_assumptions: Foundation only (no AppKit or SwiftUI); NSLock plus @unchecked Sendable for cross-actor access
Swift Concurrency async/await with URLSession.shared.data(from:)
Assumes outbound HTTPS to www.youtube.com is permitted (sandbox network client entitlement on macOS)
feature_notes: Recognized hosts after stripping a leading "www.": "youtu.be", "youtube.com", "m.youtube.com", "music.youtube.com", "youtube-nocookie.com"; anything else returns nil

For youtu.be the id is the first path segment; for the youtube.com family the first segment must be one of "shorts", "embed", "live", "v" with a second segment present, otherwise the "v" query item is used
Video id validation (checked): at least 8 characters, and every character must be a letter, a number, "-" or "_"; a bare /watch or a playlist link fails this and is never asked about
The oEmbed request is built with exactly two query items in this order: name "url" value "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=<id>", then name "format" value "json"
Only HTTP status 200 counts; any transport error, non-200 status or decode failure records finish(id, title: nil), so the link keeps its host-and-path form and is never asked again
A whitespace-and-newline-trimmed empty title is treated as no title (returns nil and is recorded as answered)

claim(id) uses Set.insert(_:).inserted so exactly one caller performs the fetch; concurrent or repeated callers get nil immediately rather than issuing a second request. The comment notes a streaming row restarts its task on every token, so the same video must be asked only once

Title cache cap: when titles.count >= 400 the whole dictionary is cleared with removeAll(keepingCapacity: true) before inserting the new title (a full flush, not LRU eviction); the claimed set is never cleared
finish() always inserts into claimed, whether or not a title was found
cached(for:) returns nil for any URL that is not a recognized video link, without touching the network
title(forVideo:) returns the known title immediately when Store already holds one, bypassing the claim
unresolved_questions: The claimed set grows without bound and is never cleared, even when titles is flushed at 400, so after a flush previously-claimed ids can never be re-fetched; whether that is intentional is not stated
Who drives title(forVideo:) (which view or warm-up task awaits it) is not in this file; the doc comment points at RichLink.prettyTitle for the read path only
No timeout, retry or cache policy is set beyond URLSession.shared defaults

files.purpose: Block-level Markdown parser for agent output, with an incremental-reparse contract for streaming replies: it returns the parsed blocks plus how many are final (stable) and the UTF-8 offset to restart from, so a growing text only re-parses its tail. Inline styling is deliberately left to AttributedString.
key_symbols: enum MarkdownBlock: Hashable, Sendable - cases heading(level:text:), paragraph(String), code(language:code:), list(ordered:start:items:), quote([MarkdownBlock]), table(header:rows:), rule
struct MarkdownListItem: Hashable, Sendable (text: String, checked: Bool?, children: [MarkdownBlock])
MarkdownParser.Parse: Equatable, Sendable (blocks: [MarkdownBlock], stable: Int, restart: Int)
private static func parse(_ text: Substring) -> Parse
private static func parse(_ lines: ArraySlice<String>, depth:) -> (blocks: [MarkdownBlock], blockLines: [Int])
private struct ListMarker (indent, ordered, start, contentOffset, content)
private static func trimmed(_:) / listMarker(_:) / indentation(_:) / fenceMarker(_:) / headingLevel(_:) / isRule(_:) / isTableDelimiter(_:) / tableCells(_:)
calls_into: Foundation String/Substring/UTF8View APIs (split, trimmingCharacters, hasPrefix, drop(while:), prefix(while:))
No project types: this file is self-contained
state_owned: No instance state; MarkdownParser is a caseless enum of static functions
Parse carries the incremental state a caller holds between streaming flushes (blocks, stable, restart)
platform_assumptions: Foundation only; no AppKit, SwiftUI or macOS-specific API in this file, so it ports without platform work
Relies on Swift UTF8View index arithmetic (text.utf8.index(_:offsetBy:), utf8.starts(with:), utf8.distance(from:to:)) and on String/Substring value semantics
feature_notes: Streaming contract: a block counts as stable only if it starts at a line index <= lines.count - 3 (at least two lines above the last line), because the parser decides a line from that line and the next; restart is the UTF-8 byte offset of that block's first line. With no such block, stable = 0 and restart = 0 and nothing is reused

parse(_:extending:) reuses the previous parse only when previous.parse.stable > 0, the new text is strictly longer in UTF-8 bytes, and text.utf8.starts(with: previous.text.utf8); otherwise the whole text is parsed again. On reuse the result is previous blocks prefix + tail blocks, stable = previous.stable + tail.stable, restart = restart + tail.restart
Line splitting is done on the UTF-8 view, splitting on byte 0x0A and dropping a trailing 0x0D, with omittingEmptySubsequences: false and without copying the whole text first
maxDepth = 8: past 8 levels of quote or list nesting the inner lines are treated as paragraph text (both the quote branch and the list branch guard with depth < maxDepth)

Fences: both "```" and "~~~" are recognized; the marker is the full run of that character at the line start; the info string after the fence becomes the language (nil when empty); a closing line must start with the marker and consist only of that character. An unterminated fence consumes to the end of input
Headings: 1 to 6 '#' characters, and the rest of the line must be empty or start with a space; the text is then trimmed of leading and trailing characters in the set "# "
Rules: a line whose first UTF-8 byte is 0x2D ('-'), 0x2A ('*') or 0x5F ('_'), containing only that byte and spaces (0x20), with at least 3 occurrences of the marker
Quotes: consecutive lines starting with '>' are gathered, the '>' and one following space stripped, and the result parsed recursively at depth + 1

Tables: a line containing '|' whose next line is a delimiter (contains '-' and every character is in "|:- ") starts a table; the header is that line's cells; rows continue while lines are non-empty and contain '|'. Cells strip one leading and one trailing '|' then split on '|' with omittingEmptySubsequences: false, trimming whitespace from each cell
Unordered list markers: '-', '*' or '+' followed by a space or tab; contentOffset = indent + 2; start is always 1
Ordered list markers: 1 to 9 digits followed by '.' or ')' followed by a space (or end of line); start = Int(digits) ?? 1; contentOffset = indent + digits.count + 2
A list may interrupt an in-progress paragraph only when the paragraph buffer is empty, or the marker is unordered, or the ordered marker starts at 1
Task list items: a leading "[ ] " sets checked = false and a leading "[x] " (case-insensitive via text.lowercased().hasPrefix) sets checked = true; in both cases the first 4 characters are removed
Indentation counts a space as 1 and a tab as 4, stopping at the first other character

List continuation across a blank line: the blank line is absorbed as an empty child line when the next line is indented past the marker and non-empty; it is skipped when the next line is a sibling marker at the same indent and same ordering; otherwise the list ends

Inside a list item, an indented line is dropped by min(indentation(line), first.contentOffset) characters and goes to childLines, unless childLines is empty and the line is neither a list marker nor a fence, in which case the trimmed line is appended to the item's own text (lazy continuation)
An unindented continuation line joins the item's text only while childLines is empty and the line is not a heading, not a fence and does not start with '>'; otherwise the list ends there
A list ends immediately when a marker at the same or lower indent has the opposite ordering (guard marker.ordered == first.ordered else break)
Item text lines are joined with "\n" then trimmed of whitespace; paragraph lines are joined with "\n" then trimmed of whitespace and newlines, and an empty result produces no block

trimmed(_:) fast path: when the line's first and last UTF-8 bytes are both printable ASCII (> 0x20 and < 0x7F) the line is returned unchanged, skipping trimmingCharacters entirely; the comment notes this also rules out the lead byte of a Unicode space
parseList's guard returns (.paragraph(lines[start]), start + 1) when the starting line unexpectedly has no marker, so the line is never lost
unresolved_questions: Setext headings (=== or --- underlines), reference links, footnotes and raw HTML blocks are not handled; whether that is a deliberate scope limit for agent output or an omission is not stated in the file

isRule is checked before the table branch, so a line of only dashes is classified as a rule; how that interacts with a table whose delimiter row contains no '|' is not documented and cannot be settled from this file alone
MarkdownBlock has no case for images or raw HTML, so how downstream views treat those inside paragraph text is outside this file

The ordered-list interruption rule (paragraph.isEmpty || !marker.ordered || marker.start == 1) differs in wording from CommonMark's rule; no comment states which behaviour was intended for edge cases such as an unordered marker interrupting prose
